"""
Module: lru_ttl_cache
=====================

A robust, thread-safe LRU (Least Recently Used) cache implementation with Time-To-Live (TTL)
expiry support. Includes a comprehensive pytest test suite.

Features:
---------
1. LRU Eviction Policy: When the cache reaches its maximum size, the least recently used
   item is evicted to make space for new items.
2. TTL Expiry: Each cached entry has a configurable time-to-live (in seconds). Expired
   entries are lazily removed upon access and eagerly cleaned during specific maintenance
   operations.
3. Thread Safety: All public methods are protected with reentrant locks (RLock) to ensure
   safe concurrent access from multiple threads.
4. Customizable Eviction Callback: Users can provide a callback function that is invoked
   whenever an item is evicted from the cache (either due to capacity limits or TTL expiry).
5. Hit/Miss Statistics: Tracks and exposes hit/miss ratios and counts for monitoring.
6. Comprehensive Test Suite: Includes unit tests for basic functionality, edge cases,
   concurrency stress tests, and performance benchmarks.

Design Decisions:
-----------------
- We use `collections.OrderedDict` as the underlying data structure because it allows
  O(1) movement of items to the end (marking them as recently used) and O(1) removal
  of items from the beginning (evicting the least recently used).
- Expired entries are not removed immediately upon creation of the entry. Instead, they
  are removed lazily when accessed (checking TTL at access time) or during explicit
  cleanup cycles. This balances CPU usage and memory efficiency.
- Thread safety is achieved using `threading.RLock`. We use RLock instead of Lock
  to allow recursive locking if necessary, though in this implementation, single
  acquisition is sufficient for standard operations.
- The TTL is stored alongside the value in the ordered dictionary.
